# Sources

<!-- Generated by scripts/sources_doc.py from sources/*.yaml. Do not edit by hand:
     change the specs (scripts/seeds_to_sources.py tables), then run
     python3 scripts/sources_doc.py. CI fails when this file is out of date. -->

Every website and dataset the crawler knows, grouped by the part of the Voyager app it
feeds. A source that serves several parts is listed under each of them.

**1968 sources, 1422 on, 546 off.**

- **What we take**: the traveller-facing data the source gives (its `relevance.why`).
- **Licence**: *open* (free reuse with credit), *share-alike* (kept apart from other
  licences), *facts only* (facts, headline, a short excerpt and a link, never the full
  text), *API terms* (the provider's terms), *restricted* (never collected).
- **On**: whether the crawler uses it now. **Key**: whether it needs an API key.

A new source must name the app section(s) it serves and why, must be about travel, and
is added only with the owner's approval (see CONTRIBUTING.md).

**Carbon footprint** (section `carbon`, added 2026-11-19) holds the emission factors and
methods used to estimate a trip's footprint: flights (per passenger-km, cabin class, load
factors, non-CO2 effects, SAF), trains, buses, ferries, cars and taxis, hotel nights (energy
per room and grid intensity), food and activities. Most factor tables are spreadsheets,
PDFs or APIs: those sources stay off with "adapter pending" or "needs an API key" until
a reader or a key exists.

**Place facts** (section `facts`, added 2026-11-20) holds short facts about countries,
regions, cities, towns, villages and features (historical, fun, popular, record-breaking
and little-known), each one sentence in our own words with its source link. The first
readers are structured: Wikidata properties, Wikipedia "Did you know" / "On this day" /
unusual-articles hooks (share-alike, kept apart, never sent to a model) and the frozen CIA
World Factbook JSON (see docs/wiki/Place-Facts-Data.md).

Off until the owner registers a key, signs an agreement or buys a licence. The
source's notes say where to sign up and what it costs.
